items.title: Tree falls on 2 cars in Pasir Belanda, no injuries reported
items.summary: BAYAN LEPAS: A falling tree damaged two cars in Pasir Belanda here this morning. Bayan Lepas assemblyman Datuk Azrul Mahathir Aziz said the incident occurred in the morning and the fallen tree blocked part of the road. He also thanked the Penang Island City Council's Engineering Department for inspecting the area and clearing tree branches obstructing traffic on the road to Gertak Sanggul.

items.title: Rantau Panjang residents pray for Aliff ahead of title fight
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: Residents and supporters here have pledged to perform regular solat hajat (special prayers) for local Muay Thai fighter Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib as he prepares for the biggest fight of his career. The champion, better known as Aliff Rakib, made history last month when he knocked out Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao in the fifth round at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok to capture the ONE interim strawweight Muay Thai World Championship. The victory made Aliff the first Malaysian fighter to win a Muay Thai world championship belt in ONE Championship.

items.title: Zahid: Rauf given full mandate to negotiate Melaka election cooperation
items.summary: GERIK: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has been given full authority to negotiate cooperation with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election. Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expressed hoped that the negotiations would not become complicated. "Discussions about seat allocations are usually complicated.

items.title: Pakistan PM wishes Anwar speedy recovery after procedure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif today wished Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery following a medical procedure the Malaysian leader had undergone. "Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures. Datuk Dr Asri Rangga Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the prime minister's medical team, said the procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of a team of medical specialists.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends marginally lower as investors stay on sidelines
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended marginally lower on Monday, as investors largely stayed on the sidelines and adopted a wait-and-see approach amid uncertainties over US monetary policy and geopolitical developments, an analyst said. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 0.38 of a point to 1,735.37 compared with last Friday's close of 1,735.75. Turnover narrowed to 3.49 billion units valued at RM2.55 billion from 3.55 billion units valued at RM3.47 billion last Friday.

items.title: Court upholds RM169.22mil asset freeze against businessman Ricky Wong and others
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Court of Appeal today upheld a High Court order to freeze assets worth up to RM169.22 million belonging to businessman Datuk Ricky Wong Shee Kai, his mother Teh Sew Wan and their company, Wong SK Holdings Sdn Bhd. A three-member panel, chaired by Federal Court judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru and comprising Court of Appeal judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and Datuk Leonard David Shim, delivered a unanimous decision. Shim, who delivered the court's decision via Zoom, said the panel found that the High Court had the authority to grant interim and inter partes injunctions under Section 360 of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (CMSA).

items.title: PKR’s Wong Chen resigns Subang parliamentary seat, effective Aug 10, press conference Wednesday
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PKR’s Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as Subang MP, effective 5pm. He said he had met Dewan Rakyat Speaker Johari Abdul on August 5 to hand over his resignation letter, allowing parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy. “We shall also be removing the honorific title of Yang Berhormat from all our billboards, signages and correspondence by next month,” he added.

items.title: Former Thai MP detained after shooting Nonthaburi local govt official
items.summary: Nonthaburi Governor Chettha Mosikarat said the incident occurred at 11am when the suspect allegedly opened fire on PAO president Police Colonel Thongchai Yenprasert and his driver. Royal Thai Police identified the suspect as former Nonthaburi member of parliament Chalong Riawraeng, who surrendered to police and was taken to Rattanathibet Police Station for questioning. Provincial Police Region 1 commissioner Police Lieutenant General Wattana Yichin led the investigation at the police station, according to police.

items.title: [UPDATED] Wong Chen resigns as Subang MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as the Subang member of Parliament. In a Facebook post today, Wong said he had handed his resignation letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul when they met on Aug 5. The resignation takes effect at 5pm today.

items.title: Gold edges higher as Fed hike bets fade, US inflation data in focus
items.summary: Spot gold was up 0.1 per cent at US$4,345.09 per ounce, as of 0856 GMT. Prices hit their highest since June 17 on Friday after weak US nonfarm payrolls data. US gold futures rose 0.1 per cent to US$4,404.80 on Monday.

items.title: Melaka BN free to negotiate, Zahid confirms Ab Rauf empowered to lead coalition seat talks
items.summary: GERIK, Aug 10 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) has been given the green light to hold discussions with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election. As reported by Harian Metro (HM), BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had empowered Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to lead the talks in search of common ground to ensure stable governance in the state. He added that Ab Rauf, who also chairs Melaka BN and Umno state liaison body, would later present the outcome of the discussions to the coalition’s top leadership before any decision is finalised.

items.title: Housing Ministry resolves RM153b worth of sick or abandoned housing projects, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) has resolved 1,647 “sick” and abandoned private housing projects worth RM153 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 homebuyers to date, said its Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said the ministry is targeting zero abandoned housing projects by 2030 as part of the national housing sector reform agenda, supported by several mechanisms. “These mechanisms include the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH), the electronic Sale and Purchase Agreement (e-SPA), periodic audits of the Housing Development Account (HDA), and the Option to Purchase (OTP), which will be introduced later this year,” he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 here today.

items.title: Iran says Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry said Monday that a defence pact signed last week between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan was "a sign of a change in the perception" of countries in the region towards the United States. "The countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false brokers," said ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei at a weekly press conference, referring to the US, an ally of the three signatories to the pact. He also said Iran was not concerned that the pact could be aimed at Teheran, highlighting "deep religious, historical and civilisational ties" with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan.

items.title: Kind-hearted stranger helps visually impaired man see again
items.summary: "This walking stick became my eyes because I could no longer see where I was going," he said. Some days, I would not even receive a single sen," he said, holding back tears. His acts of kindness meant so much to me," said Din.

items.title: Over 600 emergency pumps ready nationwide as Malaysia braces for El Nino, says Irrigation Dept
items.summary: The portable pumps would be used to channel water supplies to agricultural areas, irrigation schemes and areas experiencing water supply disruptions, as well as to support forest and peatland fire-fighting operations with the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and relevant agencies. In line with the national water sector’s digitalisation agenda, the department uses the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and Pump Tracking System to monitor pump and water gate operations in real time, enabling disruptions or potential damage to be detected early and reducing the risk of water supply disruptions during the El Nino phenomenon. DID also works with state water supply operators to optimise the operation of water intake towers to ensure continuity of water supply to consumers,” it said.

items.title: AfD on pre-election roll in east Germany, despite economists' scepticism
items.summary: Yet with regional elections looming, Gottschligg is unconcerned by the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which wants, among other things, a greater role for conventional energy sources and less support for renewables. The AfD is polling at around 41 per cent in Saxony-Anhalt, which votes on Sept 6, and 36 per cent in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, voting on Sept 20. While in western Germany much AfD support stems from opposition to immigration, experts say that in eastern Germany, the issue matters less.

items.title: Police review CCTV footage to track man who set woman on fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from around Taman Pusat Kepong to identify and track down a man who allegedly set a 62-year-old woman on fire yesterday. Sentul acting district police chief Superintendent Jasni Zolpa said investigators were examining footage from the surrounding area to establish the suspect's movements before and after the attack. Police had earlier said the victim was in critical but stable condition.

items.title: Any Melaka BN election deal must be made official, says state party chief
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 10 — Any political agreement involving Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election must be formally decided and should not be based on speculation or discussions on social media, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said any negotiations on political cooperation should take into account various factors, including the strengths, weaknesses and advantages of each party before a decision is made. He said parties interested in forming cooperation with BN for the state election were welcome to hold negotiations, but stressed that such talks would not necessarily result in an alliance.

items.title: Three new housing laws planned as govt reviews Strata Management Act, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) plans to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (DPN) 2026-2035. Minister Nga Kor Ming said the move involves three entirely new laws: the Property Development Act, the Building Managers Act, and the Rent Tenancy Act. In parallel, the government will also revise the existing Strata Management Act 2013.

items.title: Miti continues to strengthen E&E sector to ensure Malaysia remains global technology supply player
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) will continue to empower the electrical and electronics (E&E) sector to ensure Malaysia remains an important player in the global technology supply chain. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the E&E sector is one of the important fields contributing to Malaysia's position in the global supply chain, including high-tech semiconductors, advanced sensors, and telecommunications. "This step is important given that Malaysia, especially Penang and the Northern Region, is among the major hubs for the E&E industry, semiconductors, high-tech sensors, and telecommunications.

items.title: Anwar completes laparoscopic procedure, remains under medical supervision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has completed an elective laparoscopic procedure to treat an abdominal hernia. Datuk Dr Asri Rangga Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the Prime Minister's medical team, said the procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of a team of medical specialists. "The Prime Minister has successfully undergone an elective laparoscopic surgical procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia.

items.title: PH-BN talks could be political gimmick ahead of Melaka polls - Takiyuddin
items.summary: "Regarding whether there have been negotiations between PH and BN in Melaka, I have no information about that. "It should be asked of Umno whether it is true or whether there are indeed negotiations between PH and BN," he said. Instead, we held meetings and negotiations.

items.title: Doctors confirm elective surgery success, PM Anwar Ibrahim under strict medical watch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has successfully undergone elective laparoscopic surgery to treat an abdominal para umbilical hernia, his medical team confirmed today. The procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of specialist doctors. Anwar is currently undergoing physiotherapy and remains under close observation, Datuk Dr Asri Ranga bin Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the Prime Minister’s medical team, confirmed.

items.title: Pakistan PM wishes ‘brother’ Anwar swift recovery from medical procedure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wishes Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery from a medical procedure that the Malaysian leader is slated to undergo today. “Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures. Earlier, Anwar’s Senior Press Secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said the prime minister was undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of medical specialists.

items.title: Banking veteran Azlan Hashim dies at 85
items.summary: Azlan was a long-serving board member of AMMB Holdings Bhd (AmBank) and served as its deputy chairman until his retirement in 2015. He was the younger brother to AmBank founder and former chairman Tan Sri Azman Hashim. Azlan's association with AmBank began in 1982 when he joined the board of Arab Malaysian Development Bank Bhd, now known as AmInvestment Bank Bhd.

items.title: Nga: Big data system to guide housing development next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry will introduce a big data analytics system next year to help developers determine the types, prices and locations of homes needed before launching projects. Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the initiative aimed to address the persistent mismatch between property supply and actual market demand, which was a key factor contributing to the country's property overhang. The system will consolidate data from federal, state and local authorities, including information on regional income levels and housing needs.

items.title: Greece battles new fire near Athens driven by winds
items.summary: ATHENS: A new wildfire broke out in Greece Monday morning southeast of the capital Athens, fanned by strong winds of more than 70 kilometres per hour, firefighters said. At least 172 firefighters and around 40 vehicles have been deployed to fight the blaze in Kouvaras, 60 km southeast of Athens, in the Attica region, the fire service announced on X. "Two water-bombing aircraft and four helicopters" are also taking part, the service added.

items.title: Refunds follow furore as Penang cancels 29,240 ANPR summonses, vows manual enforcement only
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) will cancel 29,240 summonses issued under the automated number plate recognition (ANPR) system between 2025 and August this year. Penang local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the city council will also refund a total RM266,160 summons payments that was received in the same period. “The ANPR summons system has been halted entirely so from now onwards, summons will only be issued manually by the enforcement officers,” he said at a press conference on the issue following public furore over limitations of the system.

items.title: DKU seeks to intervene in four Undangs' bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin have applied to intervene in a legal bid by three former Undangs and a serving one to compel the state menteri besar to sign a proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as ruler. The intervention application was filed yesterday through Messrs Halim & Ismail, ahead of the four Undangs' leave application to initiate the hearing before High Court judge Norliza Othman here today. The four — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashid, Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin and Datuk Muhammed Abdullah — filed the judicial review in July, naming the menteri besar and the state government as respondents.

items.title: Industronics faces up to US$5.15mil exposure in lawsuit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Loss-making Industronics Bhd could face a bill of up to US$5.15 million (RM21.06 million) after being sued by Bluemount Investment Fund SPC over matters arising from a loan agreement. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Industronics said the dispute stems from a loan agreement dated March 24, 2025 and also involves allegations relating to certain directors and officers. Industronics said the writ was not accompanied by a statement of claim, and the company is still assessing the full basis and particulars of the suit with its legal advisers.

items.title: Retired teacher ordered to pay RM88k for slapping student four times seven years ago
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A retired teacher was ordered by the High Court here today to pay RM88,069 in total damages to a student whom he slapped four times during a lesson seven years ago. High Court judge Datuk Mohd Rosli Yusoff made the ruling after allowing a civil suit filed by the victim, through his mother, against the teacher and three other defendants. The victim, Mohamad Adam Maidin, 21, and his mother, Noor Azleen Mohamad, 47, filed the suit against the teacher, Isamuddin Ismail, 63, who was also the school's senior assistant for administration, naming him as the first defendant.

items.title: Penang cancels 29,240 automated parking compounds
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has cancelled 29,240 parking compounds issued using the Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for parking outside designated bays. He said the compounds, issued by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) in 2025 and up to August this year, would be cancelled, while motorists who had paid could apply for refunds until Sept 30. "Penang has cancelled 29,240 parking compounds issued through the ANPR system for parking outside designated bays.

items.title: Prevention is better than cure: Govt unveils OTP exit clause to stop sick housing projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The government aims to ensure Malaysia has no abandoned housing projects by 2030, with a new Option to Purchase (OTP) mechanism expected to give developers and buyers an earlier avenue to withdraw from projects that may no longer be viable. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism was part of a broader housing reform agenda aimed at preventing projects from becoming sick or abandoned in the first place. Nga said the ministry’s special task force on private-sector sick and abandoned housing projects had resolved 1,647 such projects — as of today — involving RM153 billion and nearly 200,000 homebuyers over the past three years.

items.title: Amirudin Shari: Pakatan open to working with Bersatu, Perikatan if stability maintained
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) prioritises political stability and the people’s interests when considering any form of political cooperation with other parties or coalitions, said PH Presidential Council member Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. The PKR vice-president said PH remained open to establishing cooperation or reaching an understanding with any party or coalition that upheld these two principles. “Cooperation with any party, not just Bersatu or Perikatan Nasional (PN), can be considered, provided the underlying principles remain political stability and the well-being of the people,” he said.

items.title: The death of plastic? E-wallets now displacing credit and debit cards across Malaysia
items.summary: E-wallet usage among non-cash payment users climbed from 52 per cent in 2023 to 81 per cent in 2026 — a jump of nearly 30 percentage points. Over the same period, debit card usage fell from 76 per cent to 56 per cent, and credit card usage nearly halved, from 15 per cent down to 9 per cent. Online banking and digital transfers held comparatively steady, moving from 70 per cent to 70 per cent.

items.title: Eighth day of wildfires in Indonesian national park
items.summary: SURABAYA: Indonesian firefighters backed by helicopters and drones battled devastating flames for an eighth day Monday in a national park on Java Island where over 500 hectares have been lost, an official said. By Monday, "the fire has spread toward residential areas" in the Dingklik Valley area of the park, East Java disaster mitigation agency official Satriyo Nurseno said. Two water-bombing helicopters, several fire trucks and drones with sprinklers were aiding forest rangers and soldiers deployed to fight the flames, Satriyo added.

items.title: High Court upholds blogger Jufazli Shi’s acquittal over YouTube post against Ismail Sabri, Umno
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court here today upheld the acquittal of blogger Jufazli Shi Ahmad on two charges of posting offensive communications against former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and UMNO on YouTube and failing to provide police with the password to the account four years ago. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin upheld the Sessions Court’s decision after dismissing the prosecution’s appeal against Jufazli’s acquittal on October 18, 2024, at the end of the prosecution’s case. “After reading the appeal record, the grounds of judgment of the Sessions Court judge and the submissions of both parties, this court dismisses the appellant’s appeal and upholds the decision of the Sessions Court judge to discharge and acquit the appellant,” Aslam said.

items.title: AME Elite to build Wuxi Hyatech facility in Johor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd, through its unit Pentagon Land Sdn Bhd, has secured a project to build a 220,000 square foot manufacturing facility for Shanghai-listed Wuxi Hyatech Co Ltd in Iskandar Puteri, Johor. AME Elite said the project strengthens i-TechValley's portfolio of multinational tenants within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ). AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said the project reflects the company's ability to deliver customised industrial facilities for high-precision and advanced technology operations.

items.title: How the hard reality of climate change hit Europe's economy this summer
items.summary: FOR anyone in Europe who still thought climate change was a problem for future generations, this summer's sweltering heatwaves have brought home the reality that its costly and life-altering economic impacts have already arrived. "What makes 2026 particularly worrying from an economic perspective is that there are multiple episodes of extreme events," said University of Mannheim economist Sehrish Usman. Temperatures hit records in June and July, and the economic damage will likely exceed all previous marks, economists say.

items.title: Nga confident DAP delegates will vote for country's stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming has expressed confidence that party delegates will prioritise national stability when they vote on the party's future in the Federal Government at a special congress on Aug 16. Nga, who is also Housing and Local Government Minister, said he trusts the more than 4,000 delegates attending the congress to weigh the country's interests carefully before casting their ballots. "They will vote according to the interests of the country, safeguard the country's stability and make the wisest choice in line with the country's stability.

items.title: Bar Council: Refugee repatriation must be voluntary, individually assessed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any move to repatriate 5,000 Myanmar refugees must be voluntary and subject to individual risk assessments to ensure no one is returned to persecution or serious harm, the Malaysian Bar Council said. "The Bar Council calls upon the government to ensure that any proposal to return the 5,000 Rohingya refugees is based upon individual risk assessment to guarantee that any returns are voluntary, informed, safe and dignified," he said in a statement. Anand said the Malaysian government had itself acknowledged and accepted the principle of non-refoulement since 2015.

items.title: Storms from Dolphin soak China's east, disrupt life in Shanghai
items.summary: BEIJING: Torrential rain and storms in Typhoon Dolphin's wake have swept through several provinces in China's east, drenching the coastal region and flooding streets in Shanghai, the country's second most populated city. Its remaining rain clouds continued to soak the eastern provinces including Anhui, Jiangsu and Shandong on Monday. Shanghai's two airports cancelled a total of 943 flights due to the typhoon, reducing capacity by nearly 40 per cent, state broadcaster CCTV said.

items.title: Taiwan 'throttles' mobile internet for first time during annual war games
items.summary: TAICHUNG: Taiwan slowed the mobile internet in a large swathe of the central part of the island on Monday for the first time during annual war games, simulating communication disruption in the event of a Chinese attack or natural disaster. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future. Earlier on Monday, Taiwan's military simulated repelling a Chinese air landing assault on the strategically vital Penghu Islands.

items.title: Selangor govt to local councils: Don’t let land go idle, put it to use for urban farming
items.summary: State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said applications could be made to lease the identified land for urban farming activities, including community gardens and programmes carried out by the private sector. He said the move would enable vacant urban land to be managed more systematically while optimising its use for high-value agricultural activities. “The state government has directed local government authorities (PBT) to identify idle land and apply for leases so that the sites can be utilised for community gardens, agricultural programmes or by interested private parties.

items.title: Sarawak schools told to suspend outdoor activities if API exceeds 100
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 10 — All schools in Sarawak have been urged to continuously monitor Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in their respective areas amid the transboundary haze currently affecting the state. It said in areas where API readings exceeded 100, all outdoor activities involving students must be suspended. The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.

items.title: Five men remanded another week over murder of Batu Pahat businessman found in fishing net
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 10 — Five men, who are being investigated in connection with the murder of a businessman here, have been remanded for another week. Their remand is to assist investigators who are probing the murder of a 39-year-old businessman whose bound body was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong in Parit Raja here last week. Their initial remand application ended today.

items.title: Terengganu MB says Jalur Gemilang flown without crescent moon and star was ‘unintentional’, ‘isolated’ incident
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the display of a Jalur Gemilang without its crescent and star at Dataran Batu Buruk was an isolated incident and was not deliberate. Berita Harian reported that he said the state government would investigate the matter after a video of the flag circulated on social media on Friday. He said MBKT would stop using stitched flags of that type and would instead buy fully finished flags to reduce the risk of a similar incident.

items.title: Chief secretary to govt wishes Anwar happy 79th birthday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar today wished Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a happy 79th birthday. He also prayed that the Prime Minister will always be blessed with good health, strength and wisdom in leading the country. Meanwhile, the Malaysia Madani Facebook page also prayed that the Prime Minister would always be under Allah SWT’s protection.

items.title: Bukit Aman busts violent kidnapping syndicate preying on foreigners, discovers unknown victim after shootout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department said today it succeeded in taking down a violent kidnapping syndicate that preyed on foreign nationals following a joint investigation with the Singapore Police Force. The crackdown culminated in a shootout between police and suspects, leading to the rescue of two abducted victims — a Singaporean national who works as a retirement consultant, and a Chinese national woman. Following the raid, CID director Commissioner Datuk M. Kumar said six individuals in their 30s comprising five men and one woman were arrested.

items.title: Govt unveils housing policy shift, big data to cut oversupply and drive affordable homes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Housing development will be planned according to local needs and market demand starting next year to reduce unsold homes under the new National Housing Policy 2026-2035 (DRN 2026-2035). Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the shift towards more data-driven planning was among the key changes under the policy, which seeks to address the mismatch between housing supply and demand while expanding access to affordable home ownership. “Starting next year, housing development will be planned according to local needs, location and market demand.

items.title: Penang court acquits four men over iron rod attack on lawyer
items.summary: Magistrate Nadratun Naim Mohd Saidi made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Koay Beng Ghee, 38, Teh Eng Tat, 38, Ng Weng Kooi, 43, and Yeoh Ee Seong, 48, at the close of the prosecution’s case. The court also found inconsistencies in the prosecution’s case, resulting in a failure to establish the elements of the charge against Koay, Teh and Ng, who are marketing executives, and Yeoh, a businessman. “The prosecution submitted 42 exhibits and called nine witnesses to testify.

items.title: Sanusi says Kedah may hold Penang ‘lease’ claim until Perikatan takes Putrajaya
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said the state is considering delaying its claim for higher Penang “lease” payments, and instead wait for a Perikatan Nasional (PN) takeover of the federal government. According to The Star , Sanusi said Putrajaya had yet to respond positively to Kedah’s demand despite the state pursuing a review of the payments for the past six years. “If the federal government remains stubborn and refuses to pay or consider Kedah’s application, we will change the federal government,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Penang grants Jelutong landfill extension until Oct 2026, project faces scrutiny over EIA concerns
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang state government has granted PLB Engineering Berhad (PLBE) an extension of time (EOT) until October 18 for its proposed RM1 billion Jelutong landfill rehabilitation and development project. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the developer’s application for an extension was presented to the state executive council on August 5. “Based on the presentation, the state government decided that an extension of time be granted until October 18, 2026,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: High Court requests decision on venue for judicial review involving Negeri Sembilan Undang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court has ordered counsel for three former Negeri Sembilan Undang and the incumbent Johol Undang to decide whether their judicial review will proceed here or Seremban, to avoid the risk of conflicting rulings on the same matter. High Court judge Norliza Othman’s directive follows an earlier originating summons filed by the applicants at the Seremban High Court in May, which has yet to be heard, The Edge reported. During the proceedings, the court also declined an oral application by Mohd Khairul for a gag order to prohibit public discussion of the case.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah unveils RM12.3m Penang STEM programme, targeting 100,000 students by 2030
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The federal government will allocate RM12.3 million for a four-year STEM talent programme in Penang aimed at reaching 100,000 students by 2030. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the allocation will support the implementation of the Penang STEM Talent Blueprint, which was first introduced by Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow in 2024. The programmes were developed by Tech Dome Penang, Penang Math Platform, Penang Science Cluster and Penang STEM.

items.title: Anthony Loke steps aside after 22 years, Arul Kumar appointed Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 10 — Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004. Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution.

items.title: Budget screening nears completion, Economy Ministry to forward 2027 development proposals to MoF
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Economy Ministry expects to complete its screening of development expenditure proposals for 2027 by the middle of this month, before submitting its recommendations to the Finance Ministry (MoF), Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. He said the ministry is currently in the final stage of Budget screening as part of preparations for the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). Akmal said the Budget preparation process goes through several stages, including submissions from the respective implementing ministries.

items.title: Two boys reported missing last night found drowned at Pasir Gudang dam after overnight search
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Aug 10 — The bodies of two primary schoolboys, who had been reported missing since last night, were recovered at a dam here by Fire and Rescue Department personnel early this morning. Pasir Gudang fire and rescue station operations commander Haizrul Rahmad said a water rescue team recovered Mohammad Haikal’s body at a depth of two metres and a distance of three metres from the dam’s edge at 2.12am. Haizrul said the search and rescue operation, involving fire and rescue personnel from the Pasir Gudang and Skudai stations, ended at 3am.

items.title: Transboundary haze worsens as nine Sarawak areas record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 10 — The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning. Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141). API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
